title: a terracotta window played like a drum kit
story: Ponte pa lo tuyo at ~117 BPM (onset autocorrelation lag 16 ticks; the tempo map's beats 15-17 ticks, not the report's 112): afro percussion in a 2-bar loop whose second half carries slap rolls that get denser bar by bar (8602-8634, 8721-8755, 8864-8897) until the low drums take over at 8980 (rms 0.13→0.23, centroid 0.33→0.25). The stained-glass window is the kit: every dark low drum bulges the window from the middle and lifts the light, every bright slap deepens the glass (contrast and saturation), every mid stroke thickens the lead. Every two beats the window is re-cut between organic and grid panes in a 4-step cycle that restarts with each 2-bar loop, the panes get smaller at each loop restart, and the shake on the drums escalates bar by bar over the last four bars. On the drop the window blows out, the panes go big and start to breathe, and the post-roll keeps the same kit on a new 4-step cycle while the tint drifts a step each bar.
